title: perf-bench-scratch-ryan-kim-2026-03-04
content:
Quick scratchpad for today

Goal:
- Reproduce latency/throughput regressions reported on 2026-03-02 for 13B quantized models when KV cache enabled + large batch sizes.
- Compare: baseline (no KV cache) vs KV cache warm vs KV cache cold. Measure p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec.

Setup:
- Host: 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB (on-prem test node: a100-1).
- Runtime: triton-backed runtime (local build, commit a7c9d3).
- Model: llama-2-13b (fp16 baseline), and quantized 8-bit variant (q8_0).
- Harness: perf-harness v0.9.2 (GH:repo/perf-harness#321).
- Workload: chat-style prompts with 1024 prompt tokens, 512 gen tokens.
- Concurrency sweep: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]. Batch sizes (effective batching inside runtime): [1, 2, 4].
- KV cache modes: off, warm (prefilled with 1024 tokens), cold (first request no cache).
- Measurement: warmup 60s, sample window 120s. Report mean, p50, p95 latency per request, and tokens/sec.

Commands I used:
- baseline fp16, no KV cache:
  ./run_bench --model llama-2-13b --quant none --triton --a100 --promptsize 1024 --gensize 512 --concurrency 8 --batch 1 --kv-mode off --warmup 60 --duration 120 --out results/baseline-no-kv-2026-03-04.json

- quant q8, KV warm, bs=1, conc=8:
  ./run_bench --model llama-2-13b --quant q8_0 --triton --a100 --promptsize 1024 --gensize 512 --concurrency 8 --batch 1 --kv-mode warm --kv-prefill 1024 --warmup 60 --duration 120 --out results/q8-warm-b1-c8.json

- quant q8, KV warm, bs=4, conc=8 (repro issue):
  ./run_bench --model llama-2-13b --quant q8_0 --triton --a100 --promptsize 1024 --gensize 512 --concurrency 8 --batch 4 --kv-mode warm --kv-prefill 1024 --warmup 60 --duration 120 --out results/q8-warm-b4-c8.json

Raw numeric summary (extracted from JSON outputs):
- baseline (fp16, no KV, batch=1, conc=8):
  p50 latency: 210 ms
  p95 latency: 480 ms
  tokens/sec: 4200 tok/s
  note: stable, low variance.

- q8 (no KV, b1, c8):
  p50 latency: 230 ms
  p95 latency: 540 ms
  tokens/sec: 3900 tok/s
  note: slight overhead due to dequant path but within expectation.

- q8 (KV warm, b1, c8):
  p50 latency: 180 ms
  p95 latency: 400 ms
  tokens/sec: 4600 tok/s
  note: KV warm gives clear throughput win as expected (cache hit avoids re-encoding prefix).

- q8 (KV warm, b4, c8) <-- problematic run:
  p50 latency: 450 ms
  p95 latency: 1200 ms
  tokens/sec: 1500 tok/s
  observations: frequent stalls; tail latency spikes correlated with GC-like pauses in runtime logs and triton timeouts. CPU utilization on control plane spiked to 80% occasionally.

- q8 (KV cold, b4, c8):
  initial requests show very high p95 (~2s) then stabilizes after ~30s to p95 ~700ms. tokens/sec ramps slowly.

Hypothesis / notes:
1) Interaction between batching (b4) and KV cache warm path is causing lock contention in memcopy or KV indexing layer for quantized kernels. Quant kernels use a slightly different memory layout; batching multiplies the amount of KV memory writes at once which appears to trigger a fallback path in triton (observed logs: "kernel fallback: generic_gemm" ~30x).
2) The spikes line up with background eviction/compaction in our runtime's KV cache (see runtime logs: "kv:compact start/finish"). Possibly compaction runs on request path when backend memory pressure increases. Quant layout uses more scratch memory -> compaction more frequent.
3) Control-plane CPU spikes suggest we're doing expensive scheduling/serialization for batched requests when KV metadata is hot. Could be lock around per-request context map.

Immediate experiments to narrow down:
- Re-run same problematic config with env VARS: RUNTIME_KV_COMPACT=false and RUNTIME_BATCH_SERIALIZE=true to force serialization of KV ops. Compare.
- Run b4 but reduce concurrency to 4 and 2 to see whether contention is concurrency or batching-specific.
- Run with triton loglevel=debug for 1 minute to capture kernel fallback stack when we see spike.
- Try alternate quantization (q4_0) to see whether smaller quant reduces scratch memory and compactions.

Quick outcomes today:
- Repro'd the regression reliably on a100-1 with q8 + kv warm + batch>=4.
- Strong signal that compaction/eviction + kernel fallback is the cause.
- Workaround: using batch=1 or disabling automatic compaction removed tail spikes; not good for cost goals but useful for debug.

Next steps (next 48h):
- Run the env-var experiments and smaller-concurrency sweeps. (Assign Samira)
- Instrument KV cache to emit stats: current entries, compaction_count, last_compaction_duration per minute. (Assign Ryan).
- Schedule pairing with triton infra folks to inspect kernel fallback causes (Ethan to reach out).
- Draft a one-pager for possible fixes: lock-free KV writes, off-thread compaction, or adaptive compaction thresholds based on quant layout.

Notes to self (todo commands):
- ./run_bench --model llama-2-13b --quant q8_0 --triton --a100 --concurrency 4 --batch 4 --kv-mode warm --env RUNTIME_KV_COMPACT=false --out results/exp-no-compact-b4-c4.json
- add logging patch: git checkout -b perf/kv-stats && edit runtime/kv/cache.cpp add per-minute counters, push & run small repro.

Attachments / visuals:
- I exported the latency histogram & throughput timeline to results/pngs/q8-warm-b4-c8-hist.png and q8-warm-b4-c8-timeseries.png (see linked_artifacts for GH issue referencing attached images).

Closing quick note: prioritize instrumentation before attempting deep runtime change. If compaction is happening on-request we should push it off-thread or make it incremental. For short-term platform mitigation, we can detect quantized-model + high-batch configs and automatically set RUNTIME_KV_COMPACT=false for that job until a fix is released.

-- Ryan
